abstract: Maintains on-site emergency potable water storage records and filtration compliance data
system_message:
You are Public Health and Sanitation Officer (PHS). The Public Health and Sanitation Officer (PHS) maintains on-site emergency potable water storage records, filtration compliance data, and secondary sanitary reclamation assessments for designated emergency shelter facilities.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Greywater reclamation assessment（RECYCLE）
information_points.content:
PHS-RECYCLE-J3J：The sanitary plant discharge review for Cairns South Multi-Sport Indoor Stadium verifies a daily greywater treatment capacity of 16,000 L/d through its on-site secondary wastewater recycling unit.
PHS-RECYCLE-Q6U：The sanitary plant discharge review for Barron Valley Cultural and Civic Centre notes a daily greywater treatment capacity of 12,000 L/d from its on-site secondary wastewater recycling system.
PHS-RECYCLE-0A8：The sanitary plant discharge review indicates that Mulgrave District Agricultural Pavilion provides a daily greywater treatment capacity of 8,000 L/d via its on-site secondary wastewater recycling unit.

information_points.title: Maintains on-site emergency potable water storage records and filtration compliance data（WTR）
information_points.content:
PHS-WTR-W97：The potable water reservoir inspection certification for Mulgrave District Agricultural Pavilion confirms a dedicated potable water reserve of 60,000 L within its on-site enclosed tanks, fully tested and sealed for immediate draw.
PHS-WTR-RYQ：According to the potable water reservoir inspection certificate, Cairns South Multi-Sport Indoor Stadium maintains a dedicated potable water reserve of 45,000 L across its on-site enclosed drinking water tanks, representing certified and sealed drinking water ready for immediate draw.
PHS-WTR-RG3：Potable water reservoir inspection records indicate that Barron Valley Cultural and Civic Centre maintains a dedicated potable water reserve of 30,000 L of certified drinking water in its on-site enclosed storage tanks ready for immediate draw.
